data.label: 09391: Main results regional accounts, by region, contents and year
note: Figures for household consumption and household disposable income will be published on 11 March 2016.

As part of the 2024 Coordinated Benchmark Revision, the time series in the regional national accounts have been revised. For table 09797, figures have been revised back to 2020, resulting in a break in the time series from 2020 onward.

In 2017, the Regional Reform was adopted in the Norwegian parliament. From 1 January 2020, Norway went from having 18 to 11 counties. The growth rates from 2019 to 2020 in the new counties are calculated in relation to the sum of the old counties that were merged and due to the fact that some municipalities changed their county affiliation, there will be a break in the timeseries for  the affected counties.
2015: Discontinuity in service activities incidental to oil and gas.
Years 2008-2010 were removed from the table 4 March2026.
[See list over changes in regional classifications](https://www.ssb.no/offentlig-sektor/kommunekatalog/endringer-i-de-regionale-inndelingene) (in Norwegian).
. = Category not applicable. Figures do not exist at this time, because the category was not in use when the figures were collected.

15: 1 January 2019, the municipality 1567 Rindal was moved from Møre og Romsdal to Trøndelag. 1 January 2020, the municipality 1571 Halsa was moved from Møre og Romsdal to Trøndelag. 1 January 2020, the municipality 1444 Hornindal was moved from Sogn og Fjordane to Møre og Romsdal.
18: 1 January 2020, the municipality 1852 Tjeldsund was moved from Nordland to Troms og Finnmark.
21: Svalbard is not defined as a county in the legal sense, but in official statistics Svalbard is treated in the same way as the other counties in Norway.
50: 1 January 2019, the municipality 1567 Rindal was moved from Møre og Romsdal to Trøndelag. 1 January 2020, the municipality 1571 Halsa was moved from Møre og Romsdal to Trøndelag.
